source.title: Nervous system and tissue polarity dynamically adapt to new morphologies in planaria
source.location: Fig 7A 'Decapitation' blue bar; Supplementary Dataset 1 sheet 'Figure 7' row '2nd decapitation' (new DH)

stage: fragment of a 7-day-old octanol-induced worm with heads at both ends (body fragment retaining the primary head)
injury: decapitation at the base of the secondary head

intervention.timing: octanol at first cut (pharynx/pre-tail fragments) for 3 days; re-cut of the regenerated worm at day 7 after the first cut, no further drug
intervention.description: Pharynx/pre-tail fragments soaked 3 d in 127 uM octanol and selected for heads at both ends; at day 7 re-cut by decapitation at the base of the secondary head; body fragment retaining the primary head; fragment left 14 d at 20 C in water.

readout.method: count of heads (eye spots) per regenerate

notes: Per-trial % DH regenerates [82, 100, 100, 100] from Supplementary Dataset 1 (n=15 per trial stated); each converted to counts with n=15 (rounded) and summed. Several percentages are not multiples of 1/15, so true per-trial n likely differed (deaths not reported); n_total is nominal. Non-DH regenerates coded normal (single-headed) per the methods' two-category scoring. Electrical/ionic component is the original octanol induction; the re-cut is surgical. Re-cut round 2. Fig 7A legend says N=4 (5 trials listed for some new-DH rows). ADJ: passes differed only in form (per-trial counts with the stated n=15 vs unweighted mean percent; Supplementary Table 18 means agree); counts kept per the repeats rule.
remainder_quote: Fragments regenerated at 20 °C for 14 days before scoring regenerative outcomes by counting number of single-headed and double-headed regenerates.
